q-106137.name: Question 1
q-106137.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224890/assets/e1fdcc8a8ed9dd9936ade0b088a672eadea1ca9ae7b12de7ce1b1dead2c3014a.png)

Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola sketched above.
q-106137.worked_solution:
From the graph, we deduce that the roots are ${x}_{1}=-4$ and ${x}_{2}=2.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2}=\frac{(-4)+2}{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-1.$

The graph above shows a parabola. The $x$-coordinates of $A$ and $B$ are $-\frac{8}{3}$ and $\frac{11}{5},$ respectively.  Find the axis of symmetry of the parabola.

q-223659.worked_solution:
We're given that the roots of the parabola are 
 ${x}_{1}=-\frac{8}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{11}{5}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{8}{3}+\frac{11}{5})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{40}{15}+\frac{33}{15})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{7}{15})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{7}{30}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{7}{30}.$

q-30456.name: Question 5
q-30456.problem: Find the axis of symmetry for the parabola $y=(x-6)(x+3).$
q-30456.worked_solution:
From the equation $y=(x-6)(x+3),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=6$ and ${x}_{2}=-3.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6+(-3)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{3}{2}.$

x=−32

c

d

x=−92
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the equation y=(x−6)(x+3), we find that the roots of the parabola are x1=6 and x2=−3.

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

x=x1+x22=6+(−3)2=32.

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is x=32.

q-223671.name: Question 6
q-223671.problem: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=-(x+7)(2x-5)$ is $x=${{field-1}}.
q-223671.worked_solution:
From the equation $y=-(x+7)(2x-5),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-7$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{2}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-7+\frac{5}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{14}{2}+\frac{5}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{9}{2})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{9}{4}.$

q-223688.name: Question 7
q-223688.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{9}{4},$ we will set our result equal to $-\frac{9}{4}.$ 

From the equation $y=(2x+5)(2x+k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{5}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=-\frac{k}{2}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{5}{2}-\frac{k}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{5+k}{2})}{2} \\  & =-\frac{5+k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{9}{4}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{5+k}{4} & =-\frac{9}{4} \\ 5+k & =9 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{5}{12},$ we will set our result equal to $-\frac{5}{12}.$ 

From the equation $y=(3x+7)(2x-k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{7}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=\frac{k}{2}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{7}{3}+\frac{k}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{14}{6}+\frac{3k}{6})}{2} \\  & =\frac{3k-14}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=-\frac{5}{12}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3k-14}{12} & =-\frac{5}{12} \\ 3k-14 & =-5 \\ 3k & =9 \\ k & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
